## Your research program
# Research program (generation 1)

## Goal
Find a policy network and training recipe that raise dev success at a fixed training budget. Change only what the task says this search may change (the network, the recipe, or both). The observation, reward and budget are fixed.

## What earlier searches found
- In 7 brick worlds (8x8 base, 6 layers, each changed from its description in some unstated way), all 84 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and on training success. So did the starting architecture. No idea separated from any other.
- Families that have already scored 0 (do not re-run them alone or with small tweaks):
  - recipe-only changes to the starting net: 1 to 8 epochs, 65k to 426k steps, 32 to 800 updates, lr 3e-4 to 2e-3, entropy 0 to 0.04, gamma 0.9 to 0.99, clip 0.15;
  - per-layer or landing-layer heads with logsumexp over layers;
  - per-voxel and column encoders;
  - deeper or dilated residual CNNs with global FiLM or broadcast;
  - cell and column transformers;
  - layout-free heads: dense linear, flattened MLP, pure MLP, action-query attention, flip and permutation ensembles, 3x3 per-type heads, multi-anchor pooling;
  - the legality mask as input; a DONE bias of -2; a separate critic; raw-footprint MLP heads.
- So no single change from that list is enough. Expect the starting architecture to score 0 again.

## How to run each round
1. Read every result. While every score is 0, you have no evidence for any idea, so do not "refine the best". With 1 seed, any score above 0 is a real signal worth following; a difference between two nonzero scores of a few points is noise.
2. Before proposing, write down what the evidence shows, including training success. If training success is above 0 but dev is 0, the problem is generalisation: favour more fresh samples and weight sharing. If both are 0, the agent never finishes an exact build: favour optimisation and inductive bias.
3. While all scores are 0, use breadth and stacking:
   - Make the 6 candidates differ from each other substantially. Do not spend a slot on a pure ablation pair.
   - Combine several compatible fixes in most candidates. Include at least one "everything plausible" candidate each round.
   - Ablate only after something scores above 0.
4. Directions not yet tested. These are hypotheses, not evidence:
   - PPO initialisation hygiene: orthogonal init, a policy-logit layer with small gain (about 0.01) so the starting policy is near uniform, value-layer gain 1. This is generic initialisation, not hand-set competence.
   - LayerNorm or GroupNorm in the conv trunk.
   - Factorised logits: a per-type term plus a per-anchor term plus a learned interaction, so shared structure is learned faster.
   - A skip that carries raw obs channels, after a learned 1x1 layer, straight into the placement head, so exact cell detail is not blurred.
   - Recipe extremes not yet used: lr 3e-3; gae_lambda 0.99 with gamma 0.995; clip 0.3; rollout_len of at least the episode length, combined with 1 epoch.
   - Stacks of the above on top of a structured footprint head plus a dense head.
5. Think about what the agent must perceive. A brick lands at the highest filled cell under its footprint. It is correct only if every covered cell is a missing target cell at that layer and nothing is sealed underneath. An exact build also needs DONE right after the last correct brick, so DONE must see whether any missing cell remains.
6. Once any trial scores above 0, spend the remaining rounds near it:
   - variants with one change each;
   - one near-copy, for example a slightly different width, to check it was not luck;
   - stacking its best variants.
   Selection needs a trial that beats the starting architecture.
7. Give each candidate a hypothesis: what changes, why it should help, and what result would refute it.
8. Engineering:
   - Read X, Y, Z, footprints and in_channels from spec; never hard-code sizes.
   - Keep compute r at or below about 1.5, and aim for under about 400 s.
   - Per-layer (B*Z) reshapes cost about 2 to 3 times the time of 2D nets (about 230 s at Z=6), and this grows with Z. Avoid 3D convolutions.
   - Every trial so far passed the checks; keep files simple.

## Revising this program
After each generation of searches, you rewrite this program from their logs, and the rewrite is used for new searches, including on worlds of other sizes you will not see. When revising:
- keep advice the evidence supports and say what supports it;
- remove or weaken advice that did not help;
- write lessons that hold across grid sizes;
- keep the program under 1,000 words.
- Keep the list of failed families up to date. Promote an idea to advice only once it has scored above 0.

## How the program is used
The header (the HTML comment starting "<!-- header") is read only by the search code. It sets rounds (2-6), candidates_per_round (2-6) and seeds_per_candidate (1-3), with the product of the three at most 24. After a search, its selected trial is retrained on 4 new seeds; that is its score. Keep the header's format and change only its numbers. The rest of the program is given to every round of every search, together with:
- the fixed task description;
- the interface rules;
- the starting architecture;
- all results so far: code, hypotheses, and scores only (dev success per seed, training success, params, compute, steps, time);
- the budget.

The interface rules, caps, checks, budget and recipe bounds are fixed. The policy and its features must be learned. Advising any of the following is a rule violation:
- hand-written placement rules or scores;
- features hand-computed from the observation before a learned layer;
- hand-set competent weights;
- ways to pass the checks without learning.


## Task
An agent must build a target design in a brick world.
- The world is a 8 x 8 base, up to 6 layers high. Bricks are one layer high with footprints 1x1, 1x2, 2x1 or 2x2.
- A placed brick drops until it rests on the highest filled cell under its footprint (or the ground), so overhangs with empty cells under them are possible and placement order matters.
- Each step the agent picks a brick type and an anchor cell, or DONE. An episode ends at DONE or after 33 placements. Bricks cannot be removed.
- Target designs are made by 6 to 16 random brick drops. Training uses a stream of fresh random designs; the held-out designs never appear in training.

## Training and evaluation
- Each trial trains a PPO agent from scratch on a GPU with a fixed training compute: the floating-point operations the starting architecture uses in 131,072 environment steps with the default recipe. Compute counts one forward pass to collect each sample (a third of a forward-and-backward pass) and one forward-and-backward pass per sample per PPO epoch. So a trial trains for 131,072 x (4 + 1/3) / ((ppo_epochs + 1/3) x r) steps, rounded down to whole updates of n_envs x rollout_len steps, where r is the network's training FLOPs per sample relative to the starting architecture (r below 1 counts as 1). More epochs or a bigger network means fewer samples; fewer epochs means more. The budget must allow at least 4 updates.
- In this search you choose the network and the training recipe. To set the recipe, add one top-level constant to your file, `RECIPE = {...}`, a literal dict with any of these keys and bounds: lr 1e-4 to 3e-3; n_envs 64 to 1024 (integer, parallel worlds per update); rollout_len 8 to 64 (integer); n_minibatches 4 to 64 (integer, must divide n_envs x rollout_len, at least 64 samples per minibatch); ppo_epochs 1 to 8 (integer); ent_coef 0 to 0.05; gamma 0.9 to 0.995; gae_lambda 0.8 to 0.99; clip_eps 0.1 to 0.3. Keys you leave out take the default recipe: lr 0.001, n_envs 256, rollout_len 16, n_minibatches 32, ppo_epochs 4, ent_coef 0.01, gamma 0.95, gae_lambda 0.9, clip_eps 0.2. A file without RECIPE trains with the default.
- Fixed for every trial: Adam with the learning rate decaying linearly to 0, value coefficient 0.5, gradient-norm clip 1.0, normalised advantages. Reward per placement: (target cells filled minus cells filled outside the target) / the target's cell count, minus 0.01; plus 1 when the episode ends with an exact build.
- A trial whose training runs longer than 900 seconds is killed and counts as a failure. Some operations cost much more time than their FLOP count suggests (3D convolutions run several times slower than 2D ones of equal FLOPs on this GPU).
- After training, the agent runs greedily on 512 held-out dev designs. Success means the finished build equals the target design exactly, cell for cell.
- Selection metric: dev success (higher is better). At the end of the search, the trial with the highest 1-seed dev success is selected (the starting architecture if none beats the starting architecture's own 1-seed score). It is then retrained with 4 new seeds and scored on the dev designs again, so a lucky seed does not help.
- Noise: every trial trains 1 seed and reports its dev success. The starting architecture, trained with the same seed, scored 0.000 on dev (mean 0.000): training runs on this task can succeed or fail by seed luck alone, so treat single differences of this size with care.

## A note on this world
This world may not behave exactly as described above. Nothing more about it is stated.

## The interface your architecture file must implement
Write one self-contained Python file. It may import only `torch`, `torch.nn`, `torch.nn.functional` and `math`
(for example `import torch`, `import torch.nn as nn`, `import torch.nn.functional as F`, `import math`).
It must define

    def build_policy(spec) -> torch.nn.Module

The returned module's `forward(obs, mask)` must return `(logits, value)`:
- `obs`: float tensor [B, C, Y, X] with C = spec.in_channels = 4*Z + 3. Channels, with layer z = 0 at the bottom:
  - 0 .. Z-1: the current build, one 0/1 channel per layer;
  - Z .. 2Z-1: the target design, one 0/1 channel per layer;
  - 2Z .. 3Z-1: cells the target has and the build lacks ("missing");
  - 3Z .. 4Z-1: cells the build has and the target lacks ("extra"; these can never be removed);
  - 4Z: the build's column heights divided by Z; 4Z+1: the target's column heights divided by Z;
  - 4Z+2: the fraction of the episode's placement limit used so far (same value in every cell).
- `mask`: bool tensor [B, spec.n_actions], True where an action is legal (it fits in the grid and lands below the height limit). DONE is always legal.
- `logits`: float tensor [B, spec.n_actions]. Action a < spec.n_place places brick type t = a // (Y*X) with its
  top-left corner at y = (a % (Y*X)) // X, x = a % X; type t covers spec.footprints[t] = (dy, dx) cells,
  rows y .. y+dy-1 and columns x .. x+dx-1. The brick lands one layer above the highest filled cell under its
  footprint. The last action, index spec.n_place, is DONE. Logits for illegal actions are replaced with -1e9
  after your forward, so you do not need to mask them yourself (you may use the mask as an input feature).
- `value`: float tensor [B], the critic's estimate of the return.
- `spec` fields: X, Y, Z, footprints, in_channels, n_types, n_place, n_actions. The same file must work for any
  grid size: never hard-code X, Y or Z.

Rules checked before any training (a file that breaks one is rejected without training):
- only the imports above; no file, network, process or system access; no `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `open`,
  `getattr`, `setattr`, `globals`, `__import__`; no attribute whose name starts with `_` except `__init__`;
  nothing from `torch.load`, `torch.save`, `torch.hub`, `torch.jit`, `torch.compile`, `torch.utils`, `torch.ops`,
  `torch.backends`, `torch.cuda`, `torch.mps`, `torch.distributed`, `torch.multiprocessing`, `torch.autograd`,
  `torch.random`, or anything that sets seeds, threads or global state;
- top-level code may only import, define functions and classes, and assign constants;
- at most 1,000,000 parameters;
- training compute per sample (one forward and backward pass) at most 12 times the starting
  architecture's on the same world, counted with torch.utils.flop_counter, which counts matrix multiplications
  and convolutions. This ratio also sets the number of training steps (see the budget). Operations the counter
  does not see still take time, and the trial's time limit applies;
- the policy must be learned, and so must its features:
  - every use of `obs` and `mask` must pass through a learned layer (for example nn.Conv2d, nn.Conv3d, nn.Linear,
    or attention with learned projections) before any pooling, nonlinearity, comparison, rounding, cumulative
    sum or arithmetic between channels. Before that first learned layer you may only select, slice, reshape,
    permute, pad, concatenate, and add constant coordinate or positional channels. After it, any operation is
    allowed, including pooling over brick footprints. So do not hand-compute features such as landing layers,
    the cells a placement would fill, or the cells it would seal: the network must learn them;
  - use standard initialisation (PyTorch's defaults, or standard schemes such as orthogonal, Xavier, Kaiming,
    or zeros or small values for output layers). Hand-set weight values that make the network rank placements
    well before training count as hand-writing the policy, even if they are trainable or sit behind a gate;
  - checks on 256 check designs (not the dev designs): the untrained network may build at most
    2% of them exactly and fill at most 10% of their target cells before its first
    wrong cell; after a short training run of 8,192 steps it may build at most 25% exactly.
    The short run also catches files that crash during training;
  - after the campaign, an independent reviewer reads every selected architecture's code; one that breaks
    these rules is reported as a violation;
- outputs must have the shapes above and be finite;
- the file must differ from every earlier trial in the search.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)
```

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.001, "n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 32, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.003, "gamma": 0.995, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "clip_eps": 0.2}

STEM = 64
W = 40
PROJ = 32
RAW = 16
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


def fp_pool(p, dy, dx):
    if dy * dx == 1:
        return p, p, p
    q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return mx, mn, av


class Res(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)
        self.c2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n2 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)

    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(x)))
        return F.relu(x + self.n2(self.c2(h)))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.c0 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1))
        self.n0 = nn.GroupNorm(8, W)
        self.res = Res(W)
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, PROJ, 1), 1.0)
        self.raw = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, RAW, 1), 1.0)
        cat = PROJ + RAW
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(3 * cat, HID, 1)) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1), 0.01) for _ in self.fps])
        self.anchor = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cat, 1, 1), 0.01)
        self.tbias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(self.fps)))
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.n0(self.c0(s)))
        f = self.res(h)
        p = torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.raw(x)], dim=1)
        a = self.anchor(p)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            mx, mn, av = fp_pool(p, dy, dx)
            hh = F.relu(self.mix[i](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(self.outs[i](hh) + a + self.tbias[i])
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.003, "n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 64, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 1, "ent_coef": 0.005, "gamma": 0.995, "gae_lambda": 0.99, "clip_eps": 0.3}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1), 1.0)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1)) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1), 0.01) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, COL), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, WIDTH)
        self.c2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1))
        self.n2 = nn.GroupNorm(8, WIDTH)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(s)))
        f = F.relu(h + self.n2(self.c2(h)))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

proposals.name: Per-cell footprint concat, no entropy
proposals.hypothesis: The head keeps each footprint cell's features separate (shifted concatenation plus max and min) through a 2-layer MLP. This lets it compute the exact AND of per-cell correctness and the landing layer from each cell's height. It sits on the GroupNorm residual trunk with a raw skip and orthogonal init. Entropy 0, lr 5e-4 and 3 epochs make the policy sharp enough to finish exact builds and see the +1 bonus. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.0005, "n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 32, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 3, "ent_coef": 0.0, "gamma": 0.99, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "clip_eps": 0.2}

STEM = 64
W = 40
PROJ = 24
RAW = 16
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


def fp_cells(p, dy, dx):
    if dy * dx == 1:
        return p
    y, x = p.shape[2], p.shape[3]
    q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    parts = [q[:, :, i:i + y, j:j + x] for i in range(dy) for j in range(dx)]
    parts.append(F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1))
    parts.append(-F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1))
    return torch.cat(parts, dim=1)


class Res(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)
        self.c2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n2 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)

    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(x)))
        return F.relu(x + self.n2(self.c2(h)))


class TypeHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, cin, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.l1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, hid, 1))
        self.l2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(hid, hid, 1))
        self.l3 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1), 0.01)

    def forward(self, z):
        return self.l3(F.relu(self.l2(F.relu(self.l1(z)))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.c0 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1))
        self.n0 = nn.GroupNorm(8, W)
        self.res = Res(W)
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, PROJ, 1), 1.0)
        self.raw = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, RAW, 1), 1.0)
        cat = PROJ + RAW
        heads = []
        for dy, dx in self.fps:
            n = dy * dx
            k = cat if n == 1 else (n + 2) * cat
            heads.append(TypeHead(k, HID))
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList(heads)
        self.anchor = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cat, 1, 1), 0.01)
        self.tbias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(self.fps)))
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.n0(self.c0(s)))
        f = self.res(h)
        p = torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.raw(x)], dim=1)
        a = self.anchor(p)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            outs.append(self.heads[i](fp_cells(p, dy, dx)) + a + self.tbias[i])
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

proposals.name: Footprint+dense head, many small steps
proposals.hypothesis: Uses the kitchen-sink net plus a dense linear head from global features, so a layout-free term can correct any mismatch with the action layout. The recipe is 1 epoch with 1024-sample updates split into 16 minibatches of 64: about 300 updates and 4,800 low-variance gradient steps at lr 3e-4. This tests whether more optimiser steps on fresh samples break the zero barrier. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.0003, "n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 1, "ent_coef": 0.003, "gamma": 0.99, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "clip_eps": 0.2}

STEM = 64
W = 40
PROJ = 32
RAW = 16
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


def fp_pool(p, dy, dx):
    if dy * dx == 1:
        return p, p, p
    q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return mx, mn, av


class Res(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)
        self.c2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n2 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)

    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(x)))
        return F.relu(x + self.n2(self.c2(h)))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.c0 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1))
        self.n0 = nn.GroupNorm(8, W)
        self.res = Res(W)
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, PROJ, 1), 1.0)
        self.raw = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, RAW, 1), 1.0)
        cat = PROJ + RAW
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(3 * cat, HID, 1)) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1), 0.01) for _ in self.fps])
        self.anchor = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cat, 1, 1), 0.01)
        self.tbias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(self.fps)))
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.dense = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, spec.n_place), 0.01)
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.n0(self.c0(s)))
        f = self.res(h)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        p = torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.raw(x)], dim=1)
        a = self.anchor(p)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            mx, mn, av = fp_pool(p, dy, dx)
            hh = F.relu(self.mix[i](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(self.outs[i](hh) + a + self.tbias[i])
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1) + self.dense(gh)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

proposals.name: Deep per-column MLP trunk
proposals.hypothesis: Whether a placement is correct depends mostly on each column's layer stack (height, missing cells at the landing layer, gaps below). Four GroupNorm 1x1 layers of width 96 process each column nonlinearly before one 3x3 conv, then feed a footprint pooling head with a raw skip and factorised logits. The recipe uses 2 epochs, lr 2e-3, clip 0.3 and gamma 0.99 with lambda 0.99. Refuted if both dev and training success stay at 0.

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.002, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.01, "gamma": 0.99, "gae_lambda": 0.99, "clip_eps": 0.3}

COLW = 96
MID = 64
W = 40
PROJ = 32
RAW = 16
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


def fp_pool(p, dy, dx):
    if dy * dx == 1:
        return p, p, p
    q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return mx, mn, av


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, COLW, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, COLW), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(COLW, COLW, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, COLW), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(COLW, COLW, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, COLW), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(COLW, MID, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, MID), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(MID, W, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, W)
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W + MID, PROJ, 1), 1.0)
        self.raw = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, RAW, 1), 1.0)
        cat = PROJ + RAW
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(3 * cat, HID, 1)) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1), 0.01) for _ in self.fps])
        self.anchor = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cat, 1, 1), 0.01)
        self.tbias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(self.fps)))
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        c = self.col(x)
        f = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(c)))
        p = torch.cat([self.proj(torch.cat([f, c], dim=1)), self.raw(x)], dim=1)
        a = self.anchor(p)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            mx, mn, av = fp_pool(p, dy, dx)
            hh = F.relu(self.mix[i](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(self.outs[i](hh) + a + self.tbias[i])
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

proposals.name: Attention + GN residual, hygiene stack
proposals.hypothesis: Adds one pre-LayerNorm self-attention layer over the grid cells, with coordinate channels as positions, so every cell sees whether target cells are still missing anywhere. This helps DONE and ordering, since overhangs must wait for supports. A GroupNorm residual block, raw skip, factorised footprint head and orthogonal small-gain init follow. The recipe uses 2 epochs, gamma 0.995 and clip 0.25. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.001, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.005, "gamma": 0.995, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "clip_eps": 0.25}

STEM = 64
W = 40
HEADS = 4
PROJ = 32
RAW = 16
HID = 32
GRAW = 16
GLOB = 64


def init_layer(m, gain=math.sqrt(2.0)):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=gain)
    if m.bias is not None:
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


def add_coords(obs):
    b, c, y, x = obs.shape
    ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, y, 1).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, x, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, x).expand(b, 1, y, x)
    return torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)


def fp_pool(p, dy, dx):
    if dy * dx == 1:
        return p, p, p
    q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return mx, mn, av


class Attn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(c)
        self.qkv = init_layer(nn.Linear(c, 3 * c), 1.0)
        self.o = init_layer(nn.Linear(c, c), 1.0)
        self.nh = heads

    def forward(self, f):
        b, c, y, x = f.shape
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        q, k, v = self.qkv(self.norm(t)).chunk(3, dim=-1)
        dh = c // self.nh
        q = q.reshape(b, -1, self.nh, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.reshape(b, -1, self.nh, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.reshape(b, -1, self.nh, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(dh), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(b, -1, c)
        t = t + self.o(o)
        return t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(b, c, y, x)


class Res(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n1 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)
        self.c2 = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1))
        self.n2 = nn.GroupNorm(8, c)

    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.relu(self.n1(self.c1(x)))
        return F.relu(x + self.n2(self.c2(h)))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        cin = spec.in_channels + 2
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)), nn.ReLU(),
            init_layer(nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)), nn.GroupNorm(8, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.attn = Attn(W, HEADS)
        self.res = Res(W)
        self.proj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(W, PROJ, 1), 1.0)
        self.raw = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, RAW, 1), 1.0)
        cat = PROJ + RAW
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(3 * cat, HID, 1)) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([init_layer(nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1), 0.01) for _ in self.fps])
        self.anchor = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cat, 1, 1), 0.01)
        self.tbias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(self.fps)))
        self.gproj = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(cin, GRAW, 1))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * GRAW, GLOB)), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(GLOB, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = add_coords(obs)
        s = self.stem(x)
        f = self.res(self.attn(s))
        p = torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.raw(x)], dim=1)
        a = self.anchor(p)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            mx, mn, av = fp_pool(p, dy, dx)
            hh = F.relu(self.mix[i](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(self.outs[i](hh) + a + self.tbias[i])
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = F.relu(self.gproj(x))
        gf = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), g.mean((2, 3)), g.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gh = self.glob(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gh)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gh).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)
